It employs 120 machinists in its main factory, generated $2.4 million in revenue last year and winter jackets account for 30% of total sales. The company wants to survey customers about a new winter jacket range for 2027 and has chosen a sample of 400 respondents from its database of 6,500 recent buyers.

The marketing manager, newly promoted from production, must decide between random sampling — selecting 400 names using a computerised random number generator — and quota sampling, choosing respondents to match the database profile of 55% female, 45% male and 40% aged over 50. The questionnaire will be posted with a prepaid reply envelope and costs $2,000 to print and post, and results will guide the winter range launch.
